question: When a session opens or the dashboard loads and the board branch differs from the remote, what does SOBER do on its own?

options.label: Pull on its own when it is a fast-forward, otherwise remind
options.reason: The common case — a new machine, the remote ahead, nothing local unsent — fixes itself with no act and no risk: a fast-forward cannot conflict. Anything else (local commits, a diverged branch) only gets a 'N behind / M ahead, sync' line, so push and conflicts stay the human's.
options.costLater: The board can change under you without you pressing anything; the session hook pays a network fetch at startup (needs a timeout and an offline path); core needs a fast-forward-only path next to sync().

options.label: Only remind: fetch and say how far apart they are
options.reason: Nothing is written without an act. The hook and the dashboard only report ahead/behind counts.
options.costLater: The person still has to remember to act on the reminder; a reminder shown every session turns into noise that is skipped, which is how the problem started.

options.label: Run the full sync (commit, pull, push) automatically
options.reason: Nobody ever has to think about it; both directions stay current.
options.costLater: A hook has no human: a conflict mid-sync cannot be answered and leaves the board half-merged; local work is pushed without being asked; a network failure at session start becomes a board failure.
